events.title: First Presidential Inauguration Held in January
events.description: Franklin D. Roosevelt was sworn in for his second term as U.S. President, the first inauguration held on January 20 rather than March 4, following ratification of the 20th Amendment in 1933.
events.significance: Established January 20 as Inauguration Day in the United States, shortening the lame-duck period between election and taking office.

events.title: John F. Kennedy Inaugurated as 35th U.S. President
events.description: John F. Kennedy took the oath of office and delivered his inaugural address, famously urging Americans to 'ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country.'
events.significance: At age 43 he became the youngest elected U.S. president, and his speech became one of the most celebrated in American history, defining Cold War-era idealism.

events.title: Wannsee Conference
events.description: Senior Nazi officials met in a villa in Berlin's Wannsee district to coordinate the implementation of the 'Final Solution to the Jewish Question,' organizing the logistics of the systematic deportation and murder of European Jews.
events.significance: The meeting formalized and coordinated the administrative machinery of the Holocaust, and its surviving minutes serve as key evidence of Nazi genocidal planning.

events.title: Iran Releases American Hostages as Reagan Is Inaugurated
events.description: Minutes after Ronald Reagan was sworn in as the 40th U.S. president, 52 American hostages held in Iran for 444 days were released and flown out of the country.
events.significance: The release ended the Iran hostage crisis, which had shaped U.S. politics and foreign policy and contributed to Jimmy Carter's defeat in the 1980 election.

events.title: Barack Obama Inaugurated as 44th U.S. President
events.description: Barack Obama was sworn in before an estimated 1.8 million people in Washington, D.C., becoming the first African American to serve as President of the United States.
events.significance: The inauguration marked a historic milestone in American race relations and civil rights history.
